ch13.d.speed: Launch speed as a multiple of the escape speed at the launch point: 0.71 is the circular speed, 1 the escape speed. Drag the tip of the velocity arrow to change the direction
ch13.d.alt: Height of the launch point above the surface
ch13.d.predict: The whole path computed before launch (dotted)
ch13.d.areas: Areas swept by the Earth-probe line in equal times (1/12 of a period); all are equal
ch13.d.ueff: Energy diagram at the lower right: effective potential $U_\text{eff}(r)$, energy $E$ and the current $r$; where the two lines meet, $r$ is smallest or largest
ch13.o.goal.law: The single law $F = GMm/r^2$ gives circles, ellipses, parabolas and hyperbolas
ch13.o.goal.E: The sign of the mechanical energy $E = K + U$ decides the orbit: $E < 0$ bound (ellipse), $E = 0$ parabola, $E > 0$ escape (hyperbola)
ch13.o.goal.esc: Escape speed $v_\text{esc} = \sqrt{2GM/r}$: at or above it the probe never comes back, whatever the direction
ch13.o.obs.dir: Drag the tip of the velocity arrow: the direction changes the shape of the orbit, but with the same speed $E$ and the semi-major axis stay the same
ch13.o.obs.circ: 0.71 × escape speed, horizontal: a circular orbit ($v_\text{circ} = v_\text{esc}/\sqrt 2$)
ch13.o.obs.gauge: The dashed circle is the escape speed at the current position: an arrow inside it means bound, outside means escape. On an ellipse the arrow stays inside all the way round
ch13.o.obs.energy: Energy graph: $K$ and $U$ trade off while $E$ stays flat; the probe is fastest when closest
ch13.o.obs.crash: 0.5 × escape speed: the closest approach is inside the Earth, so the probe hits the surface
ch13.o.obs.kepler: Kepler's second law (settings): equal areas in equal times, a consequence of angular momentum conservation (Ch 11)
ch13.o.assume: The Earth is a fixed uniform sphere (mass $5.97\times10^{24}$ kg, radius 6371 km); no air drag, no rotation, no other bodies; probe mass 1000 kg
ch13.o.assume.num: Fourth-order symplectic (Yoshida) integration with a 2.5 s step, so $E$ stays constant over many orbits
